scope: General local-only adversarial Pass 1 over the existing Lizard mail client. Mapped attacker-controlled email through protocol ingestion, MIME/archive parsing, authentication evidence, OpenPGP, search, threading, terminal UI and the disposable Gecko-subset renderer. Confirmed pre-limit OpenPGP decompression in the software-key provider and a queue-only bidi sanitizer bypass. Rejected direct OSC injection and CalDAV DTD/entity expansion. Product source was not modified.
notes: This is the first search in a new mail-client-only index. It is methodologically compatible with but numerically independent from httpd-rs.

scope: Local-only malicious-mail-server Pass 2 over Lizard. Treated the configured TLS-authenticated IMAP/SMTP endpoint as hostile, traced server protocol bytes and message bodies through framing, parser, memory, database, filesystem, subprocess, terminal and native-renderer boundaries, dynamically tested IMAP aggregation, fuzzed IMAP and MIME parsers in release and AddressSanitizer builds, and checked current RustSec advisories. Product source was not modified.
requested_focus: malicious mail server and remote code execution
boundary_decisions: No host RCE claim was retained: parser fuzzing and boundary review found no demonstrated memory corruption, command injection, path injection or renderer-sandbox escape.
The optional unsandboxed system GnuPG provider remains an RCE-capable dependency boundary but requires a separate GnuPG vulnerability and was not counted as a client finding.
notes: This Pass-2 search and P2-A belong only to the independent mail-client index, never the httpd-rs index.
